about: Inverted index over sarth.net. index maps a token to [page, score] pairs; page is an offset into docs, score is BM25 with title, heading and description weighting, times ten and rounded. Tokens are sorted, so a prefix match works. Built by scripts/build.py.

docs.d: Founder of Third Wall Studio, and creator of the Burlap app. Brooklyn. Data engineer, artist, and musician working in AI.
Sarth Calhoun: founder of Third Wall Studio, creator of the Burlap app. Brooklyn. Data engineer, artist and musician working in AI. Key facts and frequently asked questions.
Sarth Calhoun’s CV, newest first: Third Wall Studio, the Burlap app, writing, data engineering at Reaktor and Paramount, and the music.
Third Wall Studio, the animation studio Sarth Calhoun founded in May 2025. Animation with filmmakers and artists, mixing live action, animation and generative AI, made in Burlap.
Burlap, the native Mac app Sarth Calhoun made at Third Wall Studio: an infinite canvas for visual creation and context management, connected to models from OpenAI, Google, Runway and ByteDance.
Sarth Calhoun’s small software machines: FM / 6, a six-operator synthesizer; Image Compare Workbench; Soundscape One; and Burlap. Used at Third Wall Studio.

Ingather, the control system Sarth Calhoun built for a cannabis cultivation facility between August 2021 and March 2022. Rooms and zones, fertigation and lighting routines, dosing recipes and machines. Playable demo online.

docs.t: DuckDB, where have you been all my life
docs.d: Using Claude and DuckDB to query Burlap's JSON records of genAI calls, and running the whole append-only pipeline pattern on a laptop.

docs.t: External Tables, Partitions, CTEs, Window Functions, and Partitions
docs.d: A five-part tutorial on building an append-only data pipeline on external tables: why append-only, external tables, window functions for the current truth, runtime type checking at the boundary, and living with the code.
Why you would keep every file forever instead of upserting: an append-only store makes loads idempotent, order-independent, and parallelizable.
Laying out object storage so file paths are partitions, and defining external tables over directories of CSVs, with Snowflake as the worked example.
Unique keys, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY file_date DESC) = 1, and views: surfacing the current version of every record from an append-only store.
Runtime type checking with io-ts codecs in Node streams: errors as values, async pipelines, and why validating at the boundary saves time, money, and heartache.
Reading dense, strongly typed functional TypeScript: Prettier verticality, generics, and going one concept at a time.
The mental model for SQL window functions: compare them to aggregates, PARTITION BY vs GROUP BY, ROW_NUMBER vs RANK, and why the window grows.
Views, CTEs, joins, and why a handy way to think about SQL is that everything is a table (which is also not true).
Why most day to day Pandas work is better done in SQL, with a side by side average-sales-by-category example, and where Pandas still earns its place.

docs.t: Why Python is the default for data work
docs.d: Python is the default for data work because it is what people know, plus an ecosystem (Pandas, PyTorch) written in C, C++ and CUDA. What that does and does not tell you about building pipelines.
JSONB, horizontal scaling, and the rise and fall of MongoDB: why the argument for NoSQL got harder to make until people stopped making it.

docs.t: Node vs Rails: agnostic vs batteries included
docs.d: The case that an agnostic server like Node beats batteries included, and why I am not sure I believe it.

Somersaulting Down the Slippery Slope: The OpenAI Postmortem on Sycophancy, an essay by Sarth Calhoun first published on Noisegroove on May 6, 2025: traffic lights, arbitrary updates to our cognition, and why we should demand frozen builds with versioning.

We’ve been doing hybrid production at Third Wall Studio since before anyone called it that. I made Burlap for this precise use case: Start from original art and use it to style more images, explore variations, and generate the in-betweens.
Projects made by Sarth Calhoun with other people: Third Wall Studio, Burlap, the Gralbum Collective, Book of Sarth, Lulu, Metal Machine Trio, and more.
The Gralbum Collective, founded by Sarth Calhoun in 2012 to publish gralbums: music released as interactive apps with art, animation and storytelling.
Book of Sarth, the iPad gralbum Sarth Calhoun spent two and a half years making: a graphic novel and a concept album running as one work.
How Sarth Calhoun built the track Awakening (To Blacklist) from 60-cycle hum in Ableton Live, using a frequency shifter preset called Space Birds, and matched it to a scene in The Book of Sarth.
How Sarth Calhoun and Lou Reed made music for Robert Wilson's 2011 Berliner Ensemble Lulu, then took the material to Metallica in San Francisco.
The origin of Junior Dad: Rob Wasserman bowing electric upright at Lou Reed's apartment while Sarth Calhoun processed it through Kyma.
Sarth Calhoun on forming Metal Machine Trio with Lou Reed and Ulrich Krieger at REDCAT in 2008 and recording The Creation of the Universe.

docs.t: The Creation of the Universe, ambisonic installation
docs.d: The Metal Machine Trio Blender Theater recording spatialized as a 10.1 ambisonic installation at CSULB and Cranbrook, using Arup SoundLab technology. Sarth Calhoun on what he thought of it at the time.

Yellow Pony, billed The Yellow Pony and Other Songs and Stories: two short 2009 European tours with Lou Reed and Laurie Anderson, with Sarth Calhoun on Continuum Fingerboard and live resampling of their voices.
Poughkeepsie, Joe Kelly’s 2018 short film, whose main theme is the melody of Sarth Calhoun’s “Softly Questioning” from Reflections, Vol. 1.

Hidden Books, Hidden Stories, Lou Reed’s pavilion at the New York Photo Festival, May 12 to 16, 2010, and its slideshow at St. Ann’s Warehouse, mixed and authored by Daniel Power; the festival’s upload names Sarth Calhoun.

Vivid LIVE 2010 at the Sydney Opera House, curated by Lou Reed and Laurie Anderson. Sarth Calhoun played Metal Machine Trio, a roughly fifty-person noise band at the opening, and about a dozen unplanned jams across the two weeks.

Lou Reed’s 2011 European summer tour with an eight-piece band including Sarth Calhoun on Continuum and Kyma, Rob Wasserman, Kevin Hearn, Aram Bajakian, Tony Diodore and Tony Smith. Hop Farm and Carhaix.
How Sarth Calhoun joined Lou Reed's song-based touring band to bring live processing, electronics, and fresh sounds to the music.
Lou Reed's spring 2008 U.S. tour with Sarth Calhoun, Rob Wasserman, Kevin Hearn, Mike Rathke, Steve Hunter, and Tony Smith.

Power and Serenity: six pieces of tai chi meditation music composed and performed by Lou Reed and Sarth Calhoun for Master Ren Guangyi’s DVD, on sale from July 2010. The first thing they made together.
Lucibel Crater, the Brooklyn rock and electronic trio Sarth Calhoun founded in 2005 with Leah Coloff and Paul Chuffo, and its 2008 record The Family Album.
Number19, the Brooklyn band Sarth Calhoun formed in 1999 with Leah Coloff, Tony Diodore and Mark Righter, and its album Suspension.
The origin of Sarth Calhoun’s Christmas song, sung by Michael Patrick Flanagan Smith, with words finished by Jesse Schoen, Virginia Piazza and Doron Lev. Lyrics and links.

Sarth Calhoun’s first release of improvised duets, subtitled A Noise Akin to a Flight of Deranged Swallows in Combat, featuring Exaltron, and the track whose melody came from Joe Kelly’s film Poughkeepsie.

Tetiana Khodakivska, the Ukrainian film director and editor based in New York, artist in residence at Sarth Calhoun’s Third Wall Studio.
Archie P. Valdez, illustrator, credited with Tom Hall for the illustrations of Sarth Calhoun’s The Book of Sarth (2012).
Bora Yoon, the composer and sound artist whose Sunken Cathedral was one of the first Gralbum Collective titles, and who played the launch with Sarth Calhoun in April 2014.
Billy Martin, the drummer of Medeski Martin & Wood and visual artist, whose gralbum Omnisphere was previewed at the launch of Sarth Calhoun’s Gralbum Collective in 2014.
Andrew Beck, lead programmer of The Book of Sarth app and the (gr)album platform, who worked with Sarth Calhoun on it for three years.
Alex Wyly, the artist of The Book of Sarth (credited as Alex Smith), the graphic novel and concept album app Sarth Calhoun released in 2012; now a textile and home furnishings designer.
Adam Matta, the New York beatboxer and animator, formerly of the Carolina Chocolate Drops, whose gralbum Sketches launched with Sarth Calhoun’s Gralbum Collective in 2014.
Tom Hart, the New York artist who draws subway riders during his commutes; his Train O’ Thots and Train O’ Thoughts were published by Sarth Calhoun’s Gralbum Collective in 2014 and 2015.
Joe Kelly, the comics writer and filmmaker, whose short film Poughkeepsie took its main theme from Sarth Calhoun’s “Softly Questioning.”
Sxip Shirey, the composer, performer and storyteller, who recorded two improvised duets with Sarth Calhoun in 2015 for Introspections.
Moldover, the San Francisco musician and instrument designer who coined controllerism; Sarth Calhoun has shared bills and improvised with him since the Warper Party nights of 2009.
Michael Patrick F. Smith, the folksinger, playwright and author of The Good Hand, who sings lead on Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas.”
Dom Bouffard, the London guitarist and composer: the Berliner Ensemble Lulu band, guitars on Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas,” and co-host of the podcast Beautiful Tornado.
Phil Weinrobe, the Brooklyn producer and engineer, who recorded Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas” at Figure 8 in 2015 and played banjo on it.
Marc Urselli, the Grammy-winning engineer and Chain D.L.K. founder, who reviewed The Book of Sarth in 2012 and mixed Sarth Calhoun’s “I Just Believe in Christmas.”
Scott Hampton, the New York composer who performs as Exaltron: he gave Sarth Calhoun’s Reflections, Vol. 1 its name, plays its last track, and scored Train O’ Thoughts with him.
Lou Petto, the New Jersey and New York drummer who plays on “Softly Questioning,” Sarth Calhoun’s one-take duet on Reflections, Vol. 1.
Sarth Calhoun on working with Lou Reed: Tai Chi and meditation music, the touring band, Metal Machine Trio, Lulu, and the sounds Lou asked him to invent.
Laurie Anderson, the American artist and composer who toured Yellow Pony with Lou Reed in 2009, with Sarth Calhoun standing between them resampling their voices.
Ulrich Krieger, the German saxophonist and composer who arranged Metal Machine Music for zeitkratzer and played in Metal Machine Trio with Lou Reed and Sarth Calhoun.
Sarth Calhoun on meeting bassist Rob Wasserman, touring together with Lou Reed, and the first Kyma session that became the basis of Junior Dad.
Kevin Hearn, the Barenaked Ladies keyboardist and Lou Reed’s musical director, who played alongside Sarth Calhoun in Reed’s band from 2008 to 2011 and at the Winter Garden in 2023.
Steve Hunter, the guitarist of Lou Reed’s Berlin and Rock ’n’ Roll Animal, who played beside Sarth Calhoun in Reed’s band on the spring 2008 U.S. tour and at Lollapalooza 2009.
Tony “Thunder” Smith, the drummer who held Lou Reed’s drum chair longer than anyone, and played beside Sarth Calhoun in Reed’s band from 2008 to 2011.
Aram Bajakian, the guitarist and composer who played beside Sarth Calhoun in Lou Reed’s eight-piece band on the 2011 European tour.
Shahzad Ismaily, the multi-instrumentalist and producer, who played with Sarth Calhoun in Lou Reed Drones at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in 2019 and the Winter Garden in 2023.
John Zorn, the composer and saxophonist, who played with Sarth Calhoun at the Highline Ballroom in 2008, sat in with Metal Machine Trio in 2009, and played Lou Reed Drones in 2019.
Marc Ribot, the guitarist, who played with Sarth Calhoun in the ten-piece collaboration at Noise Night, Vivid LIVE, Sydney Opera House, May 31, 2010.
Mike Rathke, Lou Reed’s principal guitarist from New York (1989), who played beside Sarth Calhoun in Reed’s band in 2008 and 2009, in a trio at the Whitney, and on “Solsbury Hill.”
Stewart Hurwood, Lou Reed’s guitar technician, who performs Lou Reed Drones with Reed’s own guitars and amplifiers; Sarth Calhoun has played in the drones in 2019 and 2023.
Robert Wilson, the director of experimental theater, 1941 to 2025, whose Berliner Ensemble Lulu (2011) carried the score Sarth Calhoun wrote with Lou Reed.
Metallica, the band whose 2011 album Lulu with Lou Reed grew from the score Sarth Calhoun wrote with Reed; Calhoun plays electronics on every track and played it with them on stage in November 2011.
Leah Coloff, the Brooklyn cellist and songwriter who sang and played in Number19, fronts Lucibel Crater, and worked on Book of Sarth with Sarth Calhoun.
Paul Chuffo, the original drummer for Gutbucket and the drummer in Lucibel Crater with Sarth Calhoun and Leah Coloff.
Mark Righter, the drummer of Number19, the band Sarth Calhoun formed in Brooklyn in 1999, and founder of Cambium Studio.
Tony Diodore, guitarist and violinist. He and Sarth Calhoun formed Number19 in 1999 and played together again in Lou Reed's band from 2011.
Rich Kulsar, the New York drummer and Grammy winner, who plays on Mike Acerbo’s The Search alongside Sarth Calhoun’s bass on “Trilby.”
Mike Acerbo, the singer-songwriter whose album The Search (2012) opens with “Trilby,” with Sarth Calhoun on bass.
Gregory Cage, of In the Loop with Mark Righter, who played with Sarth Calhoun and looped with an Electrix Repeater.
Brandt Passalacqua, who played with Sarth Calhoun and looped with an Electrix Repeater.
Carla Scaletti, the composer and inventor of Kyma, co-founder of Symbolic Sound; Sarth Calhoun beta-tested Kyma and is credited on the Kyma X startup screen.
Kurt Hebel, co-founder of Symbolic Sound and designer of Kyma’s sound engines, the Paca that Sarth Calhoun has run on stage since 2008.
